This game is a gem and I'm sad I hadn't heard of it until I stumbled upon an ad for Ultimate (missed out on the vanilla game from EGS). This game is similar to Risk of Rain 2, but is more tactical given the separate abilities between robot and frog. It's also much easier on the eyes and feels less random (less prayers to RNGesus). The risk/reward factor for saving a planet (completing a run) adds a nice challenge and indeed rewards you well with unlockable weapons, cores, etc. There's a lot to unpack in this game and I'm stoked to continue diving in. EDIT: After spending more time with this, there is more randomization than I thought BUT that is welcomed as a means of getting the proper abilities to mold your build each run, making your initial loadout important but amenable. As you go on, the difficulty increase flows nicely and makes completing runs all-the-more satisfying. Phenomenal game!

[i] Do you and your best friend have a dob/sub fantasy where one of you (Frog) rides the other (Mech)? If so, this is the kink simulator you’ve been waiting for. In all seriousness, imagine Gunfire Reborn crossed with Risk of Rain 2, with unique mechanics sprinkled throughout. [/i] [h1]📝 Main Pros, Cons, and Suggestions:[/h1] 🟩 Pros: + Best friend mode co-op is brilliant + Crossplay between Epic, Steam and Xbox + Visually striking, with particularly stylistic weather and storm effects + Switch between melee and ranged combat on the fly (each with 3 abilities) + Mix and match GERM Cores to start with a unique core skill and 2 specific abilities + Planet anomalies create unique and at times, dynamic environments and gameplay experiences + Meta progression, along with Owl’s Protection (Easy Mode) and Hardcore Mode, catering to all players + Heat system, coupled with reward icons, are an easy-to-understand indicator of planet difficulty and reward quality 🟥 Cons: - Clunky melee (specific weapons) combat - Movement isn’t as fluid as the two aforementioned games - Enemies will occasionally get stuck, or stop attacking and moving (rare) - Grammatical errors e.g. Robot Vampire ability displaying “and damage” instead of “any damage” 🏷️ Suggestions: ~ Improved text fluidity (text appears in chunks) [h1] Two bros chillin’ in a hot tub [/h1] Shoulders of Giants: Ultimate (SoG) combines the good from Gunfire Reborn and Risk of Rain 2 and builds upon it to deliver a fun experience. The main loop has you playing as a robo-mech controlled by the frog from Chrono Trigger, hopping (pun intended) from planet to planet. Your goal is to cleanse the planets, and in doing so, you are rewarded with experience and items to do the same thing again, but faster – Simple, right? Imagine the combat from Gunfire Reborn, allowing you to switch between melee and ranged on the fly, where each mode has three unique abilities. Now, couple that with the world exploration of Risk of Rain 2, adding anomalies which modify enemies and planets (including their terrain). Finally, add on top a unique approach to gameplay (best friend mode especially), with the addition of crafting and GERM Cores, and you’ve a real winner on your hands. SoG also features arena challenges, bosses with unique mechanics, objectives such as charging beacons, eliminating marked enemies or Entropy Spires (towers), and tiered equipment and skills (levels and rarity). It’s easy to see the inspiration from, and similarities to Gunfire Reborn and Risk of Rain 2 throughout the game. If you enjoyed either or are looking for a fun experience solo or co-op, SoG is a must play. 1. 好久没遇到 音效 和 BGM 做的这么差的游戏了，差到令人发指； 2. 枯燥、乏味，局内没有任何成长性，有的只是捡起随机掉落大差不差的技能； 3. 他明明可以做成6个技能+近战/远程攻击，却非要加个“切换”近战或远程，各3个技能。属实是脑子进浆糊、有大病。 4. 本游戏的乐趣在于在局外、可以切换核心（不同的1个初始技能 和 1个被动）、与武器（影响 跑步攻击、普通攻击、空中攻击 和 蓄力攻击）； 5. 幽默的配色更换、换色不换皮。基础皮丑、换啥配色都救不了； 6. 没有人会喜欢一个走路左右摇摆、简陋的胖机甲上站一只人形青蛙； 7. 几乎没有任何地图互动的纯单机游戏，逗。 ☆ 清点掉宝的单机游戏，只能在局外更改基础装备，局内除了清点掉落技能没有任何武器/技能提升。它是肉鸽、有随机性，但局内零成长性。不存在局内构筑、不存在任何互动，玩家做的只是不断清点。 ☆ 为了解锁更多不同的武器与核心而刷图，然而没有装备系统，不存在套装构筑。今天拿把手枪技能放个电在打怪，明天拿把喷子技能丢个球打怪。这难道很有趣么？ 如果它卖38以内，小品游戏范畴，以上问题迎刃而解，但它卖76。 价格没问题，但不存在价格加分、正常评价的话，就是一坨枯燥的粪便。 顺带一提，平衡是一坨屎， 给个概念这游戏的闪避，2秒冷却、闪避过程无敌，但并不好用。

Cool concept and it is fun but its super glitchy. its like they didnt think about certain interactions. for example the final boss got flung off the map with my orbit gun so i just had to shoot it as it watched me. also enemies can be really annoying an unfun. When you have a guy that deploys a barrier that you cant shoot through and 20 melee mobs that literally cannot be shot by any gun in the game it gets kinda annoying. i get that you need to melee them or use abilities but melee is super clunky. overall fun with friend but it get old quick and i doubt you could get more then 8 hrs of fun before its just the same old game. also the cut scenes are so goofy i laughed out loud at the end of the game. idk good idea but needs work for sure

Really fun concept for a game. Risk of Rain 2 gameplay, but your starting gear is acquired looter-shooter style. Lots of fun moves and combinations of builds. Seems to scale gear and enemy level for a long time, giving motivation to keep coming back. As fun as it is, it feels like it has so much potential to be expanded. Mostly just more diverse abilities. Though I get the impression that this game is sort of done being developed.

Since Risk of Rain has kinda gone a little icky with the expansion and Gearbox's Involvement. This game has proved to be a fun alternative. This game definitely needs to be shown to more people as it is very fun and it's core concept is interesting. I wish the game was slightly more polished with certain weapons and skills feeling kinda clunky, but outside of those things I think this game is neat.

The game lasts 3.5 hours. That's the entire storyline. I.e. just long enough to make it impossible to get a refund. And you will want to do it, because the game has an inflated price tag relative to the amount of content. Once the storyline is complete, you will want to get better weapons and skills to get your dream build. And after that you realize that there is no real progress. As the HEAT level increases, the mobs' HP and your gun damage simply increase. Nothing else changes. No matter what level you are, mobs are killed with the same number of shots from a gun of the corresponding level. Even if its level does not match, you will simply spend more time. Many compare the game to Risk Of Rain - no, it's not that. Every run is always the same here. Oh yeah, online is close to zero. Network game search is useless here.

I would suggest waiting for the sale. [/td] [/tr] [/table] [h1][b]📝Story/Plot without spoilers:[/b][/h1] In Shoulders of Giants, you control a mech and a frog working together to save the universe from the forces of Entropy. The story centers around cleansing corrupted planets and restoring light to the galaxy. While the plot is minimal and more of a backdrop for the action, the narrative’s charm comes from its quirky characters, including a psychic Owl guide who adds flavor to the lore. It’s a simple yet serviceable setup that gives the gameplay some context, though it lacks the depth seen in more story-driven games. [h1][b]🎮Gameplay:[/b][/h1] [b]Dual-Control Combat System[/b] The game’s defining feature is its unique dual-character control system, where you simultaneously manage both a frog and a mech. The frog is quick, agile, and armed with a range of firearms, making it ideal for picking off enemies from a distance. Meanwhile, the mech is a hulking powerhouse, equipped with a variety of melee weapons like swords and hammers. The interplay between these two characters is fluid and engaging. You can switch between the frog and mech on the fly, using the frog for precision and ranged attacks while the mech deals massive melee damage. This dual approach makes every battle feel dynamic, as you constantly balance the different strengths and weaknesses of each character. [b]Roguelike Progression and Randomised Levels-[/b] As with many roguelikes, Shoulders of Giants is all about growth and progression through randomised stages. You’ll hop from planet to planet, each one featuring different layouts, hazards, and enemy types. As you defeat enemies, you gain experience and unlock new abilities for both the frog and the mech. This loop of growing stronger and taking on tougher challenges is addictive. Levels are procedurally generated, meaning that no two runs are the same, and each playthrough offers a fresh set of challenges. The game also features a meta-progression system that lets you upgrade your characters’ base stats and unlock new weapons and abilities that carry over between runs. Plus you will also get side quests along with the main story. [b]Abilities, Loadouts, and Customisation-[/b] Where Shoulders of Giants excels is in its ability system. Each character has access to a range of unique abilities that can be mixed and matched to suit your preferred playstyle. For example, the frog can use rapid-fire weapons for quick, precise shots or equip grenades for area control. The mech, on the other hand, has options for powerful melee attacks, shields, or crowd-control abilities. The customisation isn’t as deep as some of the genre’s heavyweights, but there’s enough variety to keep things interesting. The GERM Core system adds another layer of complexity, letting you tailor your build even further by adding perks and stat bonuses. [b]The Heat System and Difficulty-[/b] Planets come in different difficulty tiers, represented by the amount of heat gain. Higher-heat planets are more dangerous, with tougher enemies and more environmental hazards, but they also offer greater rewards. Players can choose to tackle these higher-risk planets for the chance to earn better loot. Additionally, you also get the option to play the game with 2 additions, owl’s protection and hardcode mode. Owl’s protection is for players seeking a mode casual experience. You will get reduced incoming damage and will get an extra boost when you lose multiple planets in a row. On the other hand, hardcore mode is for players who really wanna challenge themselves. Once you die, your save will be deleted and you will have to start fresh. [b]Co-op and Multiplayer Dynamics-[/b] The game supports both local and online co-op, allowing players to team up and take on planets together. The two-player mode lets one player control the frog while the other pilots the mech, leading to intense teamwork and communication. There’s also a four-player mode, where each player controls their own frog-mech duo, adding even more chaos to the battlefield. While the four-player mode can feel a bit overwhelming, the core mechanics translate well, making it a great experience whether you’re playing solo or with friends. [b]Combat Flow and Tactical Elements-[/b] The combat is fast-paced and satisfying, with a focus on tactical movement and ability management. Both the frog and the mech have dashes, grapples, and other mobility options that let you dodge incoming attacks and reposition quickly. Mastering these movement tools is crucial, especially on higher-difficulty planets where enemies swarm you relentlessly. The game’s combo system, which lets you chain together attacks from both characters, feels fluid and rewarding, making it a joy to pull off complex maneuvers. [h1][b]📷Graphics:[/b][/h1] Visually, Shoulders of Giants is a mixed bag. It’s bright, vibrant, and full of explosive colors that match the game’s high-energy vibe. The character designs are charming, especially the frog-mech duo, but the environments sometimes lack depth and detail. The levels can feel a bit repetitive visually, though the different color palettes and effects do help to differentiate between planets. Overall, the game’s art style won’t be for everyone—it’s bold and cartoonish, which may not appeal to those looking for a more refined aesthetic. [h1][b]📝Main Pros and Cons:[/b][/h1] [b]Pros-[/b] [list] [*]Unique dual-character control system keeps combat fresh and engaging. [*]Exciting co-op modes that make the game perfect for playing with friends. [*]A variety of weapons, abilities, and power-ups to experiment with. [*]Satisfying, fast-paced combat that blends melee and ranged attacks. [/list] [b]Cons-[/b] [list] [*]Art style and environment design may not appeal to everyone. [*]Levels, though randomised, can become repetitive after long sessions. [/list] [h1][b]😇Honest Rating:[/b][/h1] Overall, Shoulders of Giants is a fresh and fun take on the roguelike genre, with its unique dual-character control system, satisfying combat, and engaging co-op gameplay. The graphics and narrative might not blow you away, but the core gameplay loop is addictive, and the randomised levels ensure you’ll keep coming back for more. It’s a game that shines brightest when played with friends but still offers plenty for solo players.
